newsitem.title: GERMANY: German '97 deficit to meet EMU target-tax group.
newsitem.headline: German '97 deficit to meet EMU target-tax group.

text.p: Germany can meet the tough budget deficit target for European monetary union (EMU) this year if it maintains strict fiscal discipline, the country's taxpayers association said on Friday.
But, the association said in a statement, the national debt will still rise at an alarming rate of 3,171 marks per second in 1997, 12 percent less than the 3,605 mark per second increase in 1996.

The total public sector deficit, planned at 100 billion marks ($63.64 billion), will be 2.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997, within the three percent required for EMU qualification, the association said.
But it added total state borrowing would climb to 61 percent in 1997, from 60.5 percent in 1996, and above the 60 percent level laid down in the Maastricht treaty.
Germany's total national debt reached 2.12 trillion marks on January 1, 1997, up from 2.01 trillion the same time the year before, the association said.
Interest payments on the national debt would total 142.5 billion marks in 1997, six percent more than in 1996. ($1=1.5711 Mark)
